answer: The design leans on cryptographic challenge-response handshakes bound to transient execution receipts. Each submission hangs on the tide of a task receipt, and the mirror is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a mathematical clarity, compound sentences linking proof generation to verification register, it stays short. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the crystal of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
